headline: Dense urban district in Baku with four metro stations and paved roads

tags.reason: The transport index is 60 against the Baku median of 55.5, supported by 4 metro stations and 37 bus routes.
Commercial property stands at 2,681 AZN per m² with 0.86 shopping centres per 10,000 residents against the median of 0.39.

summary: Nizami is a compact district with a population density of 9,310 people per km², well above the Baku median of 2,890.5. The road infrastructure index is 73, with 95.4% of known roads paved compared to the median of 83.1%. Daily amenities are constrained, reflected in a convenience index of 36 versus the median of 51.5 and a healthcare index of 27. From 6,592 recorded listings, 78% have a title extract (çıxarış), with secondary flats priced at 2,231 AZN per m².
strengths: Known road network has a higher paving rate than the municipal average (95.4% paved; Baku median 83.1%)
Shopping centre density is more than double the municipal figure (0.86 malls per 10,000 residents; Baku median 0.39)
Public transit access is strengthened by underground connections (4 metro stations; transport index 60 against median 55.5)
weaknesses: Pharmacy density is less than half the metropolitan standard (1.02 pharmacies per 10,000 residents; Baku median 2.24)
Grocery store provision per capita is below average (6.98 groceries per 10,000 residents; Baku median 13.41)
Preschool capacity per capita is lower than the city benchmark (1.66 kindergartens per 10,000 residents; Baku median 2.32)
best_for: Commuters requiring rail transit across 4 metro stations
Buyers prioritising verified documentation, with 78% of listings holding a title extract (çıxarış)
watch_out: Road surface status is unrecorded for 58.9% of the road network
Industrial land cover accounts for 14.7% of the total 19.9 km² area
confidence_note: OpenStreetMap coverage is high and residential prices are based on a sample of 6,592 listings; however, land price at 32,000 AZN per sot is mock demo data and should be disregarded.
